s01.narrative: The ministers repeat the confession — at Solemn Mass the deacon and subdeacon, otherwise the servers; the faithful join them, aloud at a dialogue Mass or in spirit.

s02.translation: I confess to almighty God, to blessed Mary ever Virgin, to blessed Michael the Archangel, to blessed John the Baptist, to the holy Apostles Peter and Paul, to all the Saints, and to you, father:

s03.translation: that I have sinned exceedingly in thought, word and deed:

s04.narrative: They strike their breast three times — a visible gesture of contrition accompanying the words of self-accusation.

s05.translation: through my fault, through my fault, through my most grievous fault.

s06.translation: Therefore I beseech blessed Mary ever Virgin, blessed Michael the Archangel, blessed John the Baptist, the holy Apostles Peter and Paul, all the Saints, and you, father, to pray for me to the Lord our God.

w001.function: A deponent verb: passive in form, active in meaning. It opens the prayer and governs the long chain of datives that follows — I confess: to whom?

w002.function: Dative: the one confessed to (I confess — to whom? to God). First of the chain of datives after “confíteor”. Compare “Deum” (w065) — the same word in the accusative, in a different role.

w003.function: Third-declension adjective in the dative — agrees with “Deo”.

w005.function: Dative: the next addressee of the confession in the list after “confíteor”.

w006.function: An adverb modifying a noun, unusually: “semper Virgo” — “ever Virgin” — a fixed Marian title treated as a unit.

w007.function: Dative of the third declension (virgo, vírginis).

w008.function: Dative masculine — agrees with the name that follows, “Michaéli”.

w009.function: Dative of a name declined on the third declension (Míchael, Michaélis).

w010.function: Apposition to “Michaéli”: to Michael — the Archangel. Same case, because an apposition inherits the case of the noun it restates.

w011.function: Dative masculine — agrees with the following “Joánni”. “Beatus” recurs before each name in this litany of saints.

w013.function: Apposition to “Joánni”. A curiosity: a first-declension noun (like “María”), yet masculine — the same pattern as “agrícola”, farmer.

w015.function: Dative plural, second declension — the list of addressees continues.

w016.function: Apposition to “Apóstolis” — the Apostles named one by one, still in the dative.

w018.function: Apposition to “Apóstolis”, dative of the second declension.

w020.function: An adjective used as a noun: “(to all) the Saints” — a common move in ecclesiastical Latin.

w021.function: Coordinating conjunction — closes the list and adds its last member: the priest who is present.

w022.function: Dative of “tu”. Closes the chain of addressees: I confess also to you — the priest at the altar.

w023.function: Vocative — direct address to the priest. Hence “pater”, not the dative “patri”: this is a direct address to the person, not another item in the list.

w024.function: In ecclesiastical Latin “quia” often introduces the content of a confession or speech — “that”. Classical Latin more often means “because”; both shades resonate here: I confess that / for I have sinned.

w025.function: Perfect, 1st person singular: a completed act whose effect endures — hence the confession.

w027.function: Ablative, answering “by what means have I sinned?”. First of three ablatives of means: by thought, by word, by deed.

w028.function: Ablative of means: “by word, by speech”.

w030.function: Ablative of means (opus, óperis — third declension): “by deed”.

w031.function: Possessive in the ablative — agrees with “culpa”.

w032.function: Ablative of cause: literally “through my fault”. The written form does not distinguish the nominative (culpă) from the ablative (culpā) — sense decides: this names the cause of the sin, not the subject of a sentence. The familiar English “through my fault” renders it exactly.

w033.function: Possessive in the ablative, agreeing with “culpa” — the second of the three repetitions.

w034.function: Ablative of cause — “through my fault”. The repetition intensifies the confession.

w035.function: Possessive in the ablative agreeing with “culpa” — the third and strongest repetition: “máxima” is about to join it.

w036.function: Superlative of “magnus”: “greatest”. Agrees with “culpa” in the ablative.

w037.function: Ablative of cause. The threefold “mea culpa” builds: fault — fault — greatest fault.

w038.function: “Therefore” — the prayer's logical turn: having confessed, I now ask for intercession.

w039.function: The prayer's second deponent verb (like “confíteor”). It takes an accusative of the person plus an infinitive: I beseech whom? — to do what? Hence the whole list of saints now returns in the accusative.

w040.function: Accusative — agrees with “Maríam”. Compare “beátæ” (w004): the same word stood in the dative after “confíteor”; after “precor” the list shifts to the accusative.

w041.function: Accusative: no longer the addressee of a confession (dative) but the one beseeched to intercede (object of “precor”). Compare “Maríæ” (w005).

w042.function: Adverb inside the fixed title “semper Virgo” — “ever Virgin” — as in the first half of the prayer.

w043.function: Accusative of the third declension. Compare “Vírgini” (w007) — the dative of the same formula.

w047.function: Accusative masculine — agrees with the following “Joánnem”.

w049.function: Apposition to “Joánnem”, accusative of the first declension — a masculine first-declension noun, the same pattern as “agrícola”, farmer.

w056.function: Adjective used as a noun, accusative. Compare “Sanctis” (w020).

w058.function: Accusative of the pronoun — “you”. Compare “tibi” (w022): the same person (the priest), a different case for a different role.

w059.function: Vocative — the direct address to the priest, repeated from the first half of the prayer; hence “pater”, not “patri”.

w060.function: Infinitive in the construction “precor + accusative + infinitive”: I beseech them to pray. It carries the content of the petition.

w061.function: Preposition governing the ablative: “for, on behalf of”.

w064.function: Accusative after “ad”. The whole phrase “Dóminum Deum nostrum” stands in the accusative.

w065.function: Apposition to “Dóminum”: the Lord — God. Compare “Deo” (w002): the same word opened the prayer in the dative; the bracket closes the whole.

w066.function: Possessive in the accusative masculine — agrees with “Deum”.
